messages:
maria_cs: Weekly capacity check — noticed an unusual spike in reserved GPU hours overnight. 24h saturation hit ~95%, queue depth peaked at 42. Avg gen latency climbed to ~320ms (target <250ms). Error rate 1.8% (target <0.5%). Top tenants: tenant-helix and tenant-polara. Quick query below:

maria_cs: ```sql
SELECT tenant, sum(gpu_hours) AS gpu_hours_24h, max(queue_depth) AS max_q, avg(latency_ms) AS avg_lat
FROM reserved_usage
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY tenant
ORDER BY gpu_hours_24h DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

maria_cs: results: helix 420h / q=32 / lat=410ms, polara 210h / q=42 / lat=290ms, acme 56h / q=4 / lat=180ms

aj_ops: seeing the same. Alerts fired at 02:14UTC. Looks correlated with the nightly sweep cron for model-evals. I pulled the job list: `model-sweep` and `mass-rerank` both ran >12h.

leo_infra: dump from scheduler logs — helix-eval submitted a large batched job at 01:50UTC with batch_size=4096 (oops). Snippet:

leo_infra: ```
[2026-03-19T01:50:12Z] submit job tenant=tenant-helix name=helix-eval batch_size=4096 tokens=1.2B estimated_gpu_hours=180
[2026-03-19T01:52:03Z] job-dispatched pool=dedicated-us-west-2-gpu-rtg
[2026-03-19T02:10:45Z] start step 1/120
```

sam_se: that batch_size is massive — likely the main driver for queue depth and latency. We should ask Helix to reduce eval batch_size or run on off-peak. Short-term we can throttle their queued jobs. Long-term: recommend quantized evals or smaller shards.

elaine_am: heads-up — billing noticed a 38% spend jump for Helix week-over-week. If we throttle without syncing with them we risk a churn conversation at renewal. Please flag for AM engagement.

billing-bot: Automated billing alert: tenant-helix threshold breached (monthly forecast >= 120% of committed). Invoice sentiment: at-risk.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for runtime v2.3 started 01:30UTC — not seeing errors tied to new runtime, but overlap noted.

aj_ops: action proposal: 1) immediate runtime throttle policy on tenant-helix (cap concurrent jobs to 6 and batch_size <= 1024) 2) enable pre-warm instances for polara to reduce queuing latencies 3) request AM to schedule a customer call to discuss budget/commit changes.

maria_cs: agree. Can we do (1) as emergency mitigation? Also open a high-priority support ticket so we have a traceable thread for AMs. Ticket id: CS-4527 (placeholder until SRE creates it).

leo_infra: I can push a temporary quota for helix now. Will apply cap and confirm when applied.

aj_ops: I created a runtime policy patch and will roll it to dedicated-us-west-2-gpu-rtg as a rmw (remove after 8h if stable). Patch summary: `cap_concurrent=6, max_batch_size=1024, prewarm=off` for tenant-helix. Will monitor metrics.

sam_se: I'll draft the customer note and chime in on the call. Suggest including the cost impact breakdown and options (reserved bump vs burst credits vs scheduling).

elaine_am: scheduling: pls hold until we see immediate throttle impact. If latency/backlog improves within 1 hour I'll reach out with an ask to align on committed hours. If not, we escalate to onboarding ops.

leo_infra: throttle applied at 03:06UTC. Initial metrics (03:15UTC): saturation down to 78%, queue depth down to 11, avg latency 240ms, error rate 0.6%.

maria_cs: nice — great quick response team. Can someone take the follow-ups?

aj_ops: follow-ups I will own: monitor for 6h, rollback policy if regressions, add a rule to auto-throttle if queue_depth>25 for 15m. Will update CS-4527 with logs.

sam_se: I'll finalize the two-pager with cost/runbook and share in #customer-ready by EOD.

elaine_am: I'll coordinate the customer call and flag potential renewal risk if spend remains >20% above commit for next invoice.

maria_cs: thanks all — leaving notes for next week's check: 1) consider autoscale buffer for known eval windows 2) runbook for large-batch detection 3) product doc on safe max_batch_size per model size. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Note: billing alert cleared for tenant-polara (spend within forecast).

deploy-bot: Canary finished at 04:10UTC with no regression alerts.

maria_cs: last update — CS-4527 created and assigned to aj_ops. Monitoring continues.
